Benchmark analysis: what to learn, how to learn it, what to do

For each competitor: core strategy to borrow, then hit content and tactics (what to learn), YHI POWER local action points (what to do) and expected business value.

LinkedIn

Century Yuasa (CYB): B2B trust and a people-led brand

Core strategy to borrow: B2B trust-building and a people-led brand (for LinkedIn).

Hit content and tactics (what to learn)YHI POWER local action points (what to do)
Proof of physical assets: regularly shows its local automated plant, large-volume logistics dispatch and rigorous quality inspection lines.Build an "Australia-wide warehouse network" visual identity: film smart outbound handling and full-vehicle transfers at our Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane warehouses, stressing "national dispatch, zero stock-out risk".
People-led content: senior technical engineers, regional sales reps and long-serving warehouse staff appear on camera to answer industry pain points.Launch a "Meet the Team" series: put state account managers and energy storage engineers in front of the camera to offer real technical support and product-selection advice.
Authoritative infrastructure case studies: showcases large, mission-critical UPS installations such as telecom base stations, data centres and substations.Build a CSB & Pylontech flagship case library: collect real Australian commercial solar-plus-storage microgrid and telecom backup projects to prove delivery capability.
ESG and circular economy: a compliant recycling rate of 98%, meeting Australian environmental regulations.
Expected business and conversion value

Removes performance-risk concerns for large buyers, EPC contractors and electrical consultants, and helps open high-value B2B wholesale accounts.

Facebook / LinkedIn

EnerSys Australia: hard performance data and commercial TCO

Core strategy to borrow: Hard performance data and commercial TCO calculations (for Facebook / LinkedIn).

Hit content and tactics (what to learn)YHI POWER local action points (what to do)
Extreme-environment stress tests: shows performance at -40°C, +80°C under the bonnet, heavy vibration and self-discharge decay curves.A commercial ROI calculator for energy storage: for commercial and industrial rooftops and farm microgrids, publish a model of Pylontech / Deye energy storage bill savings and payback period.
TCO return calculations: uses real financial data to show how much maintenance time and electricity a cold-chain fleet or warehouse saves each year compared with the traditional option.Proof under extreme conditions: test the cold-start (CCA) performance of Neuton Power heavy-duty and off-road batteries in the heat of the Australian interior and on corrugated red-dirt roads.
High-value technical lead capture: white papers and fleet energy-efficiency audit guides lead prospects to submit an enquiry form.A resource pack as the lead magnet: copy that points readers to download the 2026 Australian Energy Storage and Industrial Battery Selection White Paper.
Expected business and conversion value

Moves us away from a race to the bottom on hardware specs and low prices, towards premium solution selling, and directly lifts the lead-capture rate among mid-to-large commercial and industrial customers.

Facebook / Instagram

RJ Batteries: visual hooks, tradie language and practical tools

Core strategy to borrow: Visual hooks, local tradie language and practical, tool-style education (for Facebook / Instagram).

Hit content and tactics (what to learn)YHI POWER local action points (what to do)
Strong visual hooks in real scenes: batteries shown at Supercars races, in muddy 4WD recoveries and on remote caravan camping trips.Drop the brochure look entirely: stop recycling text-heavy paper flyers and adopt one mobile-first format: a big pain-point cover, three minimal troubleshooting cards and a clear call to action.
"Battery 101" troubleshooting cheat sheets: step-by-step fault-finding, multimeter checks for weak batteries and AGM vs EFB selection (highly saved and shared).Run a "Sparky's Tech Tips" series: publish one save-worthy troubleshooting card for mechanics every week.
Community warmth and a physical network: new store openings in each state and everyday pick-ups at the warehouse, which bring the brand closer to front-line installers.Lead with channel margin and worry-free warranty: for Neuton Power car batteries, pitch workshops on a "36-month warranty, very low return rate and high wholesale margin".
Expected business and conversion value

Earns high-volume organic reach through the platform algorithm, wins over front-line mechanics and small installers, and builds repeat purchasing.

Add-on: YHI POWER Social Account Diagnosis

Based on October's social media content. Both platforms follow the same structure: overall picture, content mix, what's working, main problems, other details and what to try this week.

1. Overall picture

1,434
followers
c. 13 posts
this month, about 3 a week, with a clear step-up last week (about 7 posts)
46%
events / sponsorship / community content
  • Branding is consistent: almost every post carries #YHIPower, car posts add #NeutonPower, and every post ends with the same contact details.
  • The educational posts are strong. "A higher CCA isn't always better" and "Six warning signs" are written from the workshop and dealer point of view and offer real expertise.

2. Content mix: events take up half

TypePostsContentAvg likesAvg shares
Events / sponsorship / community6 (46%)Motorbike race, golf day, Cars & Coffee (preview and recap), Pakenham expo, data centre conferencec. 14.5c. 1.5
Customer relations1Parts4 prize draw winner161
Expert advice3 (23%)CCA, six warning signs, battery health123.3
Products / services3 (23%)Warehouse delivery, VRL AGM warranty extension, Dyness energy storage10.73

Event posts get slightly more likes, but expert and product posts are shared about twice as often. In B2B, a share is closer to "someone thinks this is useful to their peers".

3. Main problems (in order of impact)

Problem 1: one account speaks to four audiences, with no clear thread

These 13 posts target: workshops, battery retailers and fleets (delivery, warranty, advice); car owners and car clubs (Cars & Coffee, motorbike race); data centre and UPS customers (CDC conference); and solar energy storage (Dyness).

LinkedIn's strength is B2B trust. Public-facing events like the "free coffee and barbecue breakfast" suit Facebook and Instagram better; on LinkedIn, one recap post with a B2B angle is enough. Data centres and energy storage are high-value businesses, but each got only one post this month, so there is no series and customers can't see that YHI is "consistently active" in these areas.

Problem 2: engagement stops at likes, with only one route to conversion

Seven posts end with the same email, phone number and website homepage, rather than a specific page. The website already has ready-made tools: the Battery Finder, the Cross Reference Guide, product brochures and data sheets. The CCA post, for example, could easily link to the selection tool or a data sheet.

Comments are almost zero. Posts read like announcements and rarely pose a question that peers can answer.

4. Other details

  • The warranty extension (24 to 36 months) is a very strong B2B selling point, but it only got a short post. Add the eligible ranges, model coverage and claims process so dealers can take it straight to their customers.
  • Hashtags: most posts use 5–8, which is a lot, and some are generic (#Networking, #GolfDay). Fewer, better hashtags work best: keep the brand tag plus 2–3 business keywords.
  • Format: mostly an image plus long copy, with only one apparent video. Try multi-page carousel PDFs for advice content, turning "Six warning signs" and a "CCA selection checklist" into formats people can save and share.
  • Partners (Bosch, Cowes Batteries, High Country 4X4 and others): check that they are tagged. When a tagged partner reposts, it is the cheapest way to reach a new audience.
  • Missing content: customer case studies or project results (such as before-and-after battery replacement projects), named technical experts on camera, and how Neuton Power differs from competitors.

5. Priorities and three things to try this week

Fix Problem 1 first, then Problem 2

Until the content thread is clear, tweaking hashtags and posting times will bring little return. Set three regular columns, one post each per week, to replace today's random mix:

  • Expert advice: CCA, battery selection, fault-finding
  • Products and policy: warranty, new products, stock
  • Industry and events: expos and sponsorships, with only a B2B-angle recap

Move public-facing event previews (such as Cars & Coffee) mainly to Facebook and Instagram, and keep only the recaps on LinkedIn.

1. Overall picture

events / sponsorship / community content
  • Consistent branding: #YHIPOWER on almost every post, with #NeutonPower on car posts.
  • Language: concise, natural English with no machine-translated feel.
  • Every title matches a LinkedIn post: each of these 12 posts has a same-topic post on LinkedIn, which has just one extra (the data centre conference).

2. Content mix

Events / sponsorship / community5 (42%)Motorbike race, golf day, Cars & Coffee preview and recap, Pakenham expo
Expert advice3 (25%)Battery care, CCA, six warning signs
Products / promotions2 (17%)Dyness energy storage, VRL AGM warranty extension

3. What's working

Cars & Coffee is a complete event chain

The preview on 14 October covered the date, time, address, number of trophies, fuel vouchers, free coffee and entry time. A recap followed on 21 October. Car owners commented, and the account replied to them using their number plates. It is the closest thing to community management this month, and because the event is held at YHI's own Wacol branch, it is an asset competitors can't copy.

Copy is already tailored to each platform

For the warranty extension, LinkedIn says "gives you more confidence when talking warranty with customers", while Facebook says "gives your everyday driving extra peace of mind". The CCA and warning-sign posts work the same way.

Good-quality advice

The CCA post corrects the "higher is always better" myth, and the six warning signs give one clear action each, which makes them practical.

4. Main problems (in order of priority)

Problem 1: the hook speaks to car owners, but the call to action speaks to trade customers (fix this first)
  • The Dyness post opens with "Thinking about home energy storage?" but ends by asking people to "contact your local YHI POWER sales representative". Ordinary households don't have a sales rep to call.
  • The CCA post is written for car owners choosing a battery, but ends with a wholesaler's enquiry email and phone number.
  • The website has a Battery Finder and a Find a Location page, which suit consumers better, yet posts link only to the homepage. Seven of the 12 posts end with the same email, phone number and homepage link.

At the other end, content for trade customers such as workshops, battery retailers and fleet operators sits on the same page as home energy storage and car show events. If YHI ships mainly through workshops and retailers, the goal of consumer content should be to help people find their nearest partner store, not to get them phoning for a quote.

Problem 2: events make up 40% of posts but leave no conversion action

Cars & Coffee went very well, but the recap has no action tied to the battery business, such as free battery testing on the day, an email sign-up for promotions, or a QR code to the Battery Finder. The goodwill from the event isn't captured, and there is no way to tell how much business it brought in.

5. Other observations

  • The product range covered is narrow.
  • There is no video.
  • Proof-style content appeared only once.
  • Posting times are worth testing.
  • Hashtags: 4–6 per post, some generic (#Networking, #GolfDay). Keep the brand tag plus 2–3 business keywords.

6. Three things to try this week

  • Standardise the call to action. Consumer posts point to the Battery Finder or Find a Location; only trade posts use the enquiry email and phone number. Add UTM parameters to links.
  • Add a battery-business action to the next event, such as "free battery testing on the day" or "scan to get a store offer", and show the results in the recap.
  • Test one short video, preferably using footage from the motorbike race or an engine start, and compare it with an ordinary image post.

Compared with LinkedIn: split the roles by platform

The tone has already been adjusted for each platform, but the topics and the posting calendar are the same, so both platforms tell the same story on the same day and neither audience's strengths are used. We recommend:

LinkedIn: trade customers, channel partners, data centre and energy storage projects.

Facebook: local community, car owner education, events and store finder.
